After the primary check is completed and the SRS airbag warning light goes off, the system enters the ignition-enabled state, and the diagnosis circuit constantly checks the system for malfunctions. If a malfunction is detected during this constant check, the SRS airbag warning light illuminates. (The warning indication for low power supply voltage goes off after the power supply voltage returns to normal.)

By switching to the diagnosis mode, the diagnosis result for the malfunction location can be displayed by the number of times the indicator light blinks. In addition, a new diagnosis function has been adopted, and the diagnostic trouble code for the malfunction location can be read by connecting a diagnostic tool to DLC3. For details on the diagnosis mode, refer to the Repair Manual.

The millimeter wave radar sensor assembly recognizes vehicles and obstacles in the vehicle's path, and the distance control computer assembly determines whether a collision is unavoidable from the position, speed and path of the object.

The distance control computer assembly sends that information via CAN communication to the ABS & traction actuator assembly (skid control computer) and the seat belt control computer, operating each control of the pre-crash safety system.

When the ABS & traction actuator assembly (skid control computer) recognizes emergency braking by the driver or determines that there is a high possibility that the vehicle will become uncontrollable (spinning, etc.), it sends that information to the seat belt control computer via CAN communication to operate the pre-crash seat belt.

ENTRY.PTXT: When the distance control computer (pre-crash safety computer) determines that a collision is unavoidable, the belt is retracted by the motor to increase the pretensioner effect.

When the skid control computer recognizes emergency braking by the driver or determines that there is a high possibility that the vehicle will become uncontrollable, the belt is retracted by the motor to increase the pretensioner effect.

When the distance control computer (pre-crash safety computer) determines that the possibility of a collision is high, brake hydraulic pressure is boosted to increase the braking effect when the brake pedal is depressed.

When the distance control computer (pre-crash safety computer) determines that there is a possibility of a collision, it warns the driver with a buzzer and display. Furthermore, when a collision is determined to be unavoidable, the brakes are applied to reduce speed even without brake operation by the driver.

ITEM.PTXT: The light control computer is a device that supplies the alternating current (AC) power required to illuminate the HID bulb.

The frequency of the AC power is several hundred Hz or more so that no flicker is perceived during illumination, and electromagnetic shielding is provided so that electromagnetic waves do not affect the vehicle radio, etc.

The light control computer achieves instant and stable illumination of the HID bulb through controls such as generating a high voltage of up to approximately 22,000V. Since this device generates high voltage, various fail-safe functions are incorporated, and consideration has also been given to ensuring reliability against heat, humidity, vibration, etc.

ENTRY.PTXT: 1. The battery voltage is converted into a high-voltage pulse (approximately 22,000V) by the light control computer in the lamp.
2. The high-voltage pulse is applied between both electrodes of the bulb, causing the xenon gas to emit light.
3. Arc discharge occurs as the temperature inside the bulb rises.
4. As the temperature rises further, the metal iodide vaporizes and separates, and the metal atoms emit light by discharge.
5. The light control computer optimally controls the power supplied to the bulb.

MECA.TITLE: Fail-safe Function of Light Control Computer

ITEM.PTXT: When a malfunction occurs in the output voltage, input voltage or lamp side voltage, the light control computer performs fail-safe as follows.

ENTRY.PTXT: When an output malfunction is detected (short, open or leak detected) and when the bulb flickers

If a malfunction occurs in the output voltage or bulb flickering continues for 60 +/- 20 seconds or more, the headlight is turned off and remains in that state until the power is turned on again (headlight switch OFF → ON or power switch (IG) OFF → ON).

If the input voltage is outside the operating voltage (10 to 16V), the headlight is turned off, and it illuminates again as soon as the input returns to the operating range. However, if the input voltage drops after illumination, the headlight remains illuminated until the voltage reaches the illumination holding limit voltage (6V or less).
If a lamp voltage malfunction is detected, the headlight is turned off and remains in that state until the power is turned on again (headlight switch OFF → ON or power switch (IG) OFF → ON).

MECA.TITLE: Precautions for Handling Light Control Computer

ITEM.PTXT: To prevent danger, caution labels have been placed on the rear side of the headlight unit and on the light control computer.
High voltage is generated at the output terminals of the light control computer, which is dangerous, so handle it with great care.
Always have discharge headlight bulbs replaced at a Toyota dealer.
Do not touch the glass and electrode parts of the bulb, as high voltage is generated there and it is dangerous.
Illuminate the bulb only after installation has been completely finished, and do not use any power source other than the vehicle.

If the following damage (see List of Examples Requiring Replacement) is found on the light control computer or headlight after a vehicle collision, etc., replace the light control computer or headlight.
When the light control computer is clearly deformed (warped, twisted, dented, dinged, cracked, chipped, etc.).
When the resin parts of the connectors or bulb socket are cracked or chipped, or the terminals are deformed.
When contact with the ground part on the reflector side is unstable due to deformation of the socket cover, etc.
When the high-voltage harness or power supply wire harness is damaged.
Note that even if the light control computer operates normally temporarily, it is not necessarily normal.

ITEM.PTXT: The ETC on-board unit provides voice guidance about tolls and records information on the ETC card; when the vehicle passes through a toll road toll gate with an ETC card inserted in the toll collection (ETC) computer assembly, the toll is charged automatically.

MECA.TITLE: Smart Entry & Start System Detection Areas

ITEM.PTXT: Request signals sent from the certification ECU are transmitted from the antennas via each oscillator, forming the electronic key detection areas. The detection areas formed by the outside antennas and the luggage room outside antenna extend approximately 0.7 to 1.0m from the front door outside handles and the center of the rear bumper.

The detection area of the outside antennas is formed by request signals transmitted periodically approximately every 0.25 seconds while parked (engine switch OFF, doors locked), detecting the approach of the electrical key (key holder). In addition, when locking the doors, it is formed when the lock switch is ON, detecting that the electronic key (key holder) is outside the cabin.
The detection area of the luggage room outside antenna is formed when the back door lock/opener switch is ON.

The cabin detection area is formed when the driver/front passenger door is opened or closed, when the brake is depressed, when the power mode changes, when the conditions for various warnings are met, and when the lock switch is ON, detecting that the electronic key (key holder) is in the cabin.

Using the customize function, either "engine can be started in the detection area of the indoor antennas (front and rear)" or "engine can be started in the detection areas of the indoor antennas (front and rear) and the luggage room inside antenna" can be selected.
Depending on the vehicle body shape, there are places where the electronic key does not operate easily.
Even if the electronic key is within the outside key detection area, it may not be detected properly if it is near the windows, door outside handles, center of the rear bumper, etc.
Even if the electronic key is within the cabin key detection area, it may not be detected properly if it is on the instrument panel, in the glove box or on the floor.
Depending on how the electronic key is held, it may not operate easily.
Under the following conditions, the electronic key detection area may become narrower or the electronic key may not be detected properly.
When the electronic key battery is depleted
When there are facilities that generate strong radio waves nearby, such as a TV tower, power plant, broadcasting station or gas station
When carrying the electronic key together with a wireless communication device such as a radio transceiver or cellular phone
When the electronic key is covered by or in contact with a metal object
When a radio wave type keyless entry system is being operated nearby
When placed near equipment that generates high voltage or noise

When carrying the electronic key in the cabin detection area, the power mode can be changed by pressing the engine switch in combination with brake operation. In addition, if the electronic key battery is depleted, the same function operates by touching the key ornament to the engine switch and operating the brake pedal and engine switch within 5 seconds after a beep sounds.
When the engine switch is pressed without depressing the brake pedal, the power mode changes in the order OFF → ACC → IG ON → OFF → (repeat).
When the engine switch is pressed while depressing the brake pedal with the shift position in "P" or "N", the engine starts.

When the vehicle is stopped and the engine switch is pressed with the shift position in "P" while the engine is running, the power mode changes to OFF. When the shift position is in any position other than "P", it changes to ACC.

If the engine start conditions are not met due to a malfunction such as a blown stop light fuse or a faulty stop light switch, the engine can be started by moving the shift position to "P", setting the power mode to "ACC" with the engine switch, then depressing the brake pedal and pressing and holding the engine switch for approximately 15 seconds or more.
Do not start the engine using the above method except in an emergency.

Because of its convenience, the Smart Entry & Start System may cause the driver to become unaware of the key. ITEM.PTXT: Because the Smart Entry & Start System forms the outside detection area by periodically transmitting request signals every 0.25 seconds, the vehicle battery may become discharged if the vehicle is left unused for a long time. Therefore, the following controls are provided to prevent battery discharge.
If there is no response from the electronic key for 5 days or more, the periodic transmission interval of request signals is extended to 0.75 seconds.
If there is no response from the electronic key for 14 days or more, periodic transmission of request signals (formation of the detection area) is stopped.

INDICATE.TITLE: Electronic Key Battery Power Saving Function

ITEM.PTXT: Even if the lock or unlock button on the electronic key is held down, transmission stops automatically after approximately 20 seconds.

If the electronic key is left in the outside detection area for a long time, the electronic key continues to transmit the ID code to the indoor tuner, which may discharge the electronic key battery. Therefore, the following controls are provided to prevent battery discharge.
If the electronic key is in the outside detection area for 10 minutes or more, periodic transmission of request signals (formation of the detection area) is stopped.
When any of the following conditions is met, the system returns from power saving control to normal Smart Entry & Start System control.
Door lock/unlock by the wireless remote control function.
Door lock/unlock by inserting the mechanical key into the driver door key cylinder.
Door lock by the smart door lock function.

When the key function is canceled, the doors can be locked/unlocked using the wireless remote control function or the mechanical key. In addition, the engine can be started by touching the ornament of the electronic key to the front of the engine switch.

When the power is changed from ON (ACC or IG ON) to OFF (ACC and IG OFF), the security indicator light in the air conditioning control panel blinks continuously at an interval of approximately 2.0 seconds (0.2 seconds ON, ON/1.8 seconds OFF), indicating that the immobiliser system is set. The security indicator light is controlled by the certification ECU.
Only when the IDs match as a result of verification is the immobiliser system released; when the engine switch is pushed, the security indicator light goes off and engine starting is permitted.

When the key battery is depleted, touching the electronic key to the engine switch causes electromagnetic waves to be generated (a magnetic field to be formed) around the engine switch. This causes the electronic key to transmit its ID code, and the certification ECU verifies it against the registered ID codes.
